title: Time of flight, range, and maximum height
problem: A ball is projected at 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. Take $g = 10$ m/s². Find (a) the time of flight, (b) the range, (c) the maximum height.

steps.instruction: Find the time of flight using $T = \dfrac{2u\sin\alpha}{g}$.

answer: (a) The time of flight is $2$ s. (b) The range is $20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.64$ m. (c) The maximum height is $5$ m.

title: Velocity at a given time
problem: A ball is projected at 25 m/s with $\sin\alpha = \tfrac{3}{5}$ and $\cos\alpha = \tfrac{4}{5}$. Take $g = 10$ m/s². Find the velocity vector and speed at $t = 2$ s.

steps.instruction: Find the horizontal velocity, which is constant.
Find the vertical velocity at $t = 2$ s using $v_y = u\sin\alpha - gt$.
steps.working: $$v_y = u\sin\alpha - gt = 25 \times \frac{3}{5} - 10 \times 2 = 15 - 20 = -5 \text{ m/s}$$ The negative value means the ball is moving downward at $t = 2$ s.

answer: The velocity vector at $t = 2$ s is $(20, -5)$ m/s, and the speed is $5\sqrt{17} \approx 20.62$ m/s.

title: Working backwards from range
problem: A ball is kicked at 45° and lands 90 m away on level ground. Take $g = 10$ m/s². Find the initial speed.

steps.instruction: Rearrange the range formula $R = \dfrac{u^2\sin 2\alpha}{g}$ to make $u^2$ the subject.
Take the square root to find $u$.

answer: The initial speed is $30$ m/s. (Note: the maximum range is achieved at 45° because $\sin 2\alpha$ is maximised when $2\alpha = 90°$, giving $R_{\max} = \dfrac{u^2}{g}$.)
